# 开源许可与第三方声明

冷咖啡原创的桌面界面、交互、客户端适配、事务式安装与恢复等代码按根目录 [MIT 许可证](LICENSE) 分发。独立组件、源代码快照、运行时、词典和第三方资料分别保留自己的许可证；根目录 MIT 许可证不覆盖这些作品。

完整版权、许可和 NOTICE 原文汇编在 [随包开源声明](desktop/resources/legal/OPEN_SOURCE_NOTICES.txt)。软件中的「关于与开源许可」提供相同内容。这些文件是归属和许可记录，不表示上游作者为冷咖啡或收费服务背书。

| 组件 | 固定版本与来源 | 随包记录与修改说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 网关核心 | [yetone/magpie](https://github.com/yetone/magpie)，0.1.3186，提交 `f9a88c4fbeec771f71f2d05fbb77ce1a6239d035`，MIT，Copyright (c) 2026 yetone | 上游二进制未修改，构建时按 SHA-256 验证；[LICENSE](desktop/resources/magpie/LICENSE)、[THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES](desktop/resources/magpie/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES) 原样保留。冷咖啡主界面及集成为独立实现，接入范围见 [集成说明](docs/MAGPIE-INTEGRATION.md)。 |
| REA 源码和运行资源 | [morluto/rea](https://github.com/morluto/rea)，源码提交 `833136507dd79d959340b09862a53af344e4f1b3`，运行资源 `rea-agents@6.7.0`，主体 MIT | [固定来源清单](desktop/resources/upstream-skills/catalog.json) 记录逐包摘要；完整源码、MIT、第三方 NOTICE、`licenses/` 和子项目许可保留在对应 `.bundle.json.gz`，安装时完整还原。REA 内的第三方作品按原许可分发。 |
| reverse-skill | [zhaoxuya520/reverse-skill](https://github.com/zhaoxuya520/reverse-skill)，准确提交与摘要见固定来源清单，主体 MIT | 完整源码和许可证保留在 `reverse-skill.bundle.json.gz`。其中 `CTF-Sandbox-Orchestrator/` 是独立 GPL-3.0 子项目，GPL 全文与对应源码完整随包分发；`skills/pentest-tools/src-hunter/` 保留 MyuriKanao 的 MIT 声明。各自归属保持独立。 |
| Grok Bot 协议参考与源码快照 | [Lniosy/souhun](https://github.com/Lniosy/souhun)，提交 `b8fb8ed08d0657cb07675f31d5110b2da4c8744b`，MIT，Copyright (c) 2026 lniosy | [说明](desktop/resources/grok-memory/NOTICE.md)、[MIT 原文](desktop/resources/grok-memory/LICENSE.souhun.txt)、完整源码归档与逐文件清单随包保留。冷咖啡界面与 Node/Electron 集成独立编写，不执行归档里的脚本。 |
| IDA 中文词典及插件 | `tools/ida-zh-cn`；词典参考 0x-focus/IDA-Pro-9.0-Chinese-Translation 与 tuxi/ida-i18n，MIT | 原始版权与 MIT 原文见 [NOTICE](tools/ida-zh-cn/NOTICE.md) 与 [LICENSE](tools/ida-zh-cn/LICENSE)。插件本体和整合文档独立实现；本项目不分发 IDA 主程序。 |
| 桌面运行依赖 | `jsonc-parser@3.3.1`（MIT）、`smol-toml@1.9.0`（BSD-3-Clause）、`yaml@2.9.0`（ISC） | 精确锁定版本、版权与许可全文纳入随包开源声明；依赖图见 `desktop/package-lock.json`。 |
| 桌面运行框架 | Electron 及其 Chromium/Node 组件 | 对应运行时的 `LICENSE.electron.txt` 与 `LICENSES.chromium.html` 随平台安装包分发，保留其原始第三方声明；不以本项目许可证替代。 |

REA 保留了上游记录的许可信息缺口和补充说明；`burp-mcp-full/` 在固定来源中没有独立许可证文件，保持来源根许可证与原记录，不虚构额外授权。第三方工具名称用于说明兼容和集成，实际下载或执行的外部工具仍适用各自条款。

完整技能来源快照以 gzip 压缩 JSON 保存；每个条目包含相对路径、原始字节的 Base64、大小和 SHA-256。还原方法及可复现工具见 [技能说明](docs/UPSTREAM-SKILLS.md) 和 `tools/vendor_upstream_skills.py`。GPL 子项目的对应源码与许可证就在同一分发物中，不依赖未来提供源码的承诺。

原画、图标与布偶猫路由角色为冷咖啡生成的原创视觉，来源参数和摘要见 `desktop/assets/brand-v6/provenance.json` 与 `desktop/assets/route-ragdoll/provenance.json`。产品名称和商标属于各自权利人；本项目与上述第三方无隶属或官方背书关系。付费 API 中转、闭源工作流和定制服务的收费说明，不改变已开源部分及第三方组件的许可权利。

# Grok Bot 记忆管理：来源与实现

上游：[Lniosy/souhun](https://github.com/Lniosy/souhun)

固定提交：`b8fb8ed08d0657cb07675f31d5110b2da4c8744b`

许可证：MIT，Copyright (c) 2026 lniosy。完整许可证见 `LICENSE.souhun.txt`。

`souhun-b8fb8ed-source.tar.gz` 完整保留此提交的全部 Git 跟踪文件，包括 Windows / macOS / Python 客户端、文档、图片和旧网页端。`source-manifest.json` 列出逐文件 SHA-256、大小以及原始源码归档的 SHA-256。归档供审计和研究，不参与应用启动，不执行其脚本。

冷咖啡实现位于 `desktop/src/lib/grok-memory/` 与 `desktop/src/workbench/grok-memory*`。界面、Electron 集成、操作预览、严格请求关联、证据阶段、取消与错误脱敏为冷咖啡独立编写；Grok Bot 的 RPC 方法、系统加密记录格式、checksum 变换与记忆操作流程参考了上述 MIT 上游。完整保留来源，不将上游作品称为冷咖啡原创。

本功能不包含 Grok Bot 程序或任何登录凭证。使用者主动连接自己的本机登录后，主进程向固定 Grok Bot 服务地址发起请求。服务变更、账号权限、模型记忆工具可用性会影响实际结果。

重建归档：检出固定提交后运行 `python tools/vendor_souhun.py --source <souhun-checkout>`。

# 第三方声明 · Third-party notices

## 哪些是原创，哪些不是

| 部分 | 来源 |
|---|---|
| `plugin/ida_zh_cn.py`（插件本体）、`install.ps1`、`tools/`、`docs/`、`assets/` 下的全部设计与文档 | 本项目原创，MIT 许可 |
| `plugin/zh_cn.json`（词典） | **主体来自下面两个 MIT 许可的社区项目**，由本项目合并、规范化，并补充了表头、窗口名、图例、工具栏与提示语等词条 |

词典共 1860 条：其中 1712 条（约 92%）的英文原文与下列两个项目的词条重合，
本项目新增 148 条。重合词条的译文由本项目在两者之间择优取用（取舍规则见 `docs/how-it-works.md`）。

没有复制这两个项目的任何程序代码：本项目的插件实现方式（绘制层翻译 + 可还原的文字替换）与它们不同，
且为独立编写。

REA uses a caller-supplied Node.js runtime ([MIT and component notices](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/LICENSE)).

OpenJDK ([GPLv2 with Classpath Exception and component notices](https://openjdk.org/legal/)),

or a Chromium-based browser ([BSD-3-Clause and third-party licenses](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/LICENSE)).
These external installations are not licensed or bundled by REA's MIT license.

Development, test, and website npm packages are included in the locked inventory.
GitHub Actions, operating-system utilities, downloaded verification fixtures,
and their runtimes retain the terms supplied by their publishers. Fixture
identities and provenance are recorded under `scripts/fixtures/` and the
existing `third_party/` records; downloaded executable fixtures are not tracked
or included in the npm package. This notice does not claim to inventory every
dependency of a caller's operating system, agent, or separately installed tool.

## Maintaining and redistributing notices

Refresh the dependency inventory and runtime notice collection when the lockfile
changes. Review the actual versions and distributed contents, retain the
upstream license and copyright texts, and account for optional platform

GCC RUNTIME LIBRARY EXCEPTION

Version 3.1, 31 March 2009

Copyright (C) 2009 Free Software Foundation, Inc. <http://fsf.org/>

Everyone is permitted to copy and distribute verbatim copies of this
license document, but changing it is not allowed.

This GCC Runtime Library Exception ("Exception") is an additional
permission under section 7 of the GNU General Public License, version
3 ("GPLv3"). It applies to a given file (the "Runtime Library") that
bears a notice placed by the copyright holder of the file stating that
the file is governed by GPLv3 along with this Exception.

When you use GCC to compile a program, GCC may combine portions of
certain GCC header files and runtime libraries with the compiled
program. The purpose of this Exception is to allow compilation of
non-GPL (including proprietary) programs to use, in this way, the
header files and runtime libraries covered by this Exception.

0. Definitions.

A file is an "Independent Module" if it either requires the Runtime
Library for execution after a Compilation Process, or makes use of an
interface provided by the Runtime Library, but is not otherwise based
on the Runtime Library.

"GCC" means a version of the GNU Compiler Collection, with or without
modifications, governed by version 3 (or a specified later version) of
the GNU General Public License (GPL) with the option of using any
subsequent versions published by the FSF.

"GPL-compatible Software" is software whose conditions of propagation,
modification and use would permit combination with GCC in accord with
the license of GCC.

"Target Code" refers to output from any compiler for a real or virtual
target processor architecture, in executable form or suitable for
input to an assembler, loader, linker and/or execution
phase. Notwithstanding that, Target Code does not include data in any
format that is used as a compiler intermediate representation, or used
for producing a compiler intermediate representation.

The "Compilation Process" transforms code entirely represented in
non-intermediate languages designed for human-written code, and/or in
Java Virtual Machine byte code, into Target Code. Thus, for example,
use of source code generators and preprocessors need not be considered
part of the Compilation Process, since the Compilation Process can be
understood as starting with the output of the generators or
preprocessors.

A Compilation Process is "Eligible" if it is done using GCC, alone or
with other GPL-compatible software, or if it is done without using any
work based on GCC. For example, using non-GPL-compatible Software to
optimize any GCC intermediate representations would not qualify as an
Eligible Compilation Process.

1. Grant of Additional Permission.

You have permission to propagate a work of Target Code formed by
combining the Runtime Library with Independent Modules, even if such
propagation would otherwise violate the terms of GPLv3, provided that
all Target Code was generated by Eligible Compilation Processes. You
may then convey such a combination under terms of your choice,
consistent with the licensing of the Independent Modules.

2. No Weakening of GCC Copyleft.

The availability of this Exception does not imply any general
presumption that third-party software is unaffected by the copyleft
requirements of the license of GCC.

                            Preamble

  The licenses for most software are designed to take away your
freedom to share and change it.  By contrast, the GNU General Public
Licenses are intended to guarantee your freedom to share and change
free software--to make sure the software is free for all its users.

  This license, the Library General Public License, applies to some
specially designated Free Software Foundation software, and to any
other libraries whose authors decide to use it.  You can use it for
your libraries, too.

  When we speak of free software, we are referring to freedom, not
price.  Our General Public Licenses are designed to make sure that you
have the freedom to distribute copies of free software (and charge for
this service if you wish), that you receive source code or can get it
if you want it, that you can change the software or use pieces of it
in new free programs; and that you know you can do these things.

  To protect your rights, we need to make restrictions that forbid
anyone to deny you these rights or to ask you to surrender the rights.
These restrictions translate to certain responsibilities for you if
you distribute copies of the library, or if you modify it.

  For example, if you distribute copies of the library, whether gratis
or for a fee, you must give the recipients all the rights that we gave
you.  You must make sure that they, too, receive or can get the source
code.  If you link a program with the library, you must provide
complete object files to the recipients so that they can relink them
with the library, after making changes to the library and recompiling
it.  And you must show them these terms so they know their rights.

  Our method of protecting your rights has two steps: (1) copyright
the library, and (2) offer you this license which gives you legal
permission to copy, distribute and/or modify the library.

  Also, for each distributor's protection, we want to make certain
that everyone understands that there is no warranty for this free
library.  If the library is modified by someone else and passed on, we
want its recipients to know that what they have is not the original
version, so that any problems introduced by others will not reflect on
the original authors' reputations.

  Finally, any free program is threatened constantly by software
patents.  We wish to avoid the danger that companies distributing free
software will individually obtain patent licenses, thus in effect
transforming the program into proprietary software.  To prevent this,
we have made it clear that any patent must be licensed for everyone's
free use or not licensed at all.

  Most GNU software, including some libraries, is covered by the ordinary
GNU General Public License, which was designed for utility programs.  This
license, the GNU Library General Public License, applies to certain
designated libraries.  This license is quite different from the ordinary
one; be sure to read it in full, and don't assume that anything in it is
the same as in the ordinary license.

  The reason we have a separate public license for some libraries is that
they blur the distinction we usually make between modifying or adding to a
program and simply using it.  Linking a program with a library, without
changing the library, is in some sense simply using the library, and is
analogous to running a utility program or application program.  However, in
a textual and legal sense, the linked executable is a combined work, a
derivative of the original library, and the ordinary General Public License
treats it as such.

  Because of this blurred distinction, using the ordinary General
Public License for libraries did not effectively promote software
sharing, because most developers did not use the libraries.  We
concluded that weaker conditions might promote sharing better.

  However, unrestricted linking of non-free programs would deprive the
users of those programs of all benefit from the free status of the
libraries themselves.  This Library General Public License is intended to
permit developers of non-free programs to use free libraries, while
preserving your freedom as a user of such programs to change the free
libraries that are incorporated in them.  (We have not seen how to achieve
this as regards changes in header files, but we have achieved it as regards
changes in the actual functions of the Library.)  The hope is that this
will lead to faster development of free libraries.

  The precise terms and conditions for copying, distribution and
modification follow.  Pay close attention to the difference between a
"work based on the library" and a "work that uses the library".  The
former contains code derived from the library, while the latter only
works together with the library.

  Note that it is possible for a library to be covered by the ordinary
General Public License rather than by this special one.

# Preserved licenses and attribution

Start with [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) for the distinction
between distributed material and separately obtained tools. These files retain
upstream texts; they do not change [REA's MIT license](../LICENSE).

| Files                                                  | Provenance and scope                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm-dependencies.txt`                                 | Every package path in the root lockfile, with its exact version, declared license, scope, download URL, and integrity. Includes development and optional platform entries.                                                                                                                |
| `npm-runtime-notices.txt`                              | Original license, copyright, and NOTICE texts collected from integrity-verified locked runtime npm archives across all platforms; also the license of Rolldown's generated runtime helpers. The archive manifest's name and version are checked.                                          |
| `nativeaot-parser-MIT.txt`                             | Original Washi notice for derived NativeAOT parser code; source revision is recorded in the parser and the root notices.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `dotnet-runtime-MIT.txt`                               | Original .NET Foundation MIT text from the NativeAOT reference revision `a3b2d40328be0be3f8dd43f0e5cc925b8827b044`.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `ghidra-12.1.4-{LICENSE,NOTICE,DISCLAIMER}.txt`        | Unchanged top-level documents from `Ghidra_12.1.4_build`. Ghidra is not bundled; these reference copies do not replace its component and GPL support-program notices. The US-government-specific disclaimer applies to Ghidra, not to REA.                                                |
| `cfworker-MIT.txt`, `xterm-MIT.txt`                    | Original notices missing from their published runtime npm archives, recovered from the releases' upstream Git revisions. They are included in the corresponding runtime entries.                                                                                                          |
| `Apache-2.0.txt`, `MIT-template.txt`                   | Standard license texts for explicitly documented upstream notice gaps. The MIT placeholders are not an attribution to an inferred author or year.                                                                                                                                         |
| `frida-17.23.2-COPYING.txt`, `LGPL-2.0.txt`            | Unchanged licensing supplements for the optional Frida dependency: tagged Frida wxWindows notice and GNU Library GPL v2 text. The npm archive and tagged Node binding omit a standalone license/copyright document; these texts do not recover binding or prebuild-component attribution. |
| `MinGW-w64-runtime.txt`                                | Upstream's combined runtime copyright and license notices, snapshot from v12.0.0, for the statically linked Windows addon. This is a notice snapshot, not a pin of the compiler used in release CI.                                                                                       |
| `GPL-3.0.txt`, `GCC-Runtime-Library-Exception-3.1.txt` | Unchanged GPLv3 and GCC runtime exception texts from GCC 14.2.0. The exception permits eligible compiled combinations under its conditions; the runtime keeps its own license. This snapshot does not assert that every release uses GCC 14.2.0.                                          |
| `Node-22.19.0-LICENSE.txt`                             | The original Node 22.19.0 license and third-party notices. The Windows addon uses Node-API headers from that release; the complete Node runtime and all components listed in this reference document are not bundled.                                                                     |
| `upstream-sources.json`                                | Source URLs and SHA-256 digests for the new unchanged reference and supplemental texts. These digests identify the preserved local texts.                                                                                                                                                 |

Additional preserved originals live at
[evmole/LICENSE](../third_party/evmole/LICENSE),
[pwndbg/LICENSE.md](../third_party/pwndbg/LICENSE.md), and
[the website dinosaur notice](../website/public/assets/licenses/dinosaur.txt).

## Collection scope and maintenance

The inventory and runtime texts were prepared from the root lockfile. The
collection downloaded the locked npm archives, checked their lockfile
integrity and package identity, and read license/NOTICE/copyright documents
without installing packages or executing lifecycle scripts. It includes
optional platform packages that may not be present in one local installation.
Temporary archives were removed after collection.

For releases that omit original documents, the collection uses pinned upstream
texts, embedded source/README license sections, or the same release's parent
notice for the `@lydell/node-pty` prebuilt family. `evmole@0.9.3` uses the existing
preserved upstream license. `clean-git-ref@2.0.1` and `minimisted@2.0.1` provide
only license and author metadata: their missing original copyright documents
remain explicitly identified in the runtime texts. Do not describe those
entries as complete recovered attribution.

`frida@17.23.2` also lacks an original standalone notice in its npm archive and
tagged Node source. Its declared license and the preserved licensing supplements
are recorded explicitly without inferring a copyright holder or year.

These records do not establish the legal accuracy of upstream metadata or
prove that every upstream source-file attribution has been supplied in an
archive. Review and refresh them when dependencies change; compare reference
texts with the sources and SHA-256 digests in `upstream-sources.json`.

When updating engines, copied code, website assets, or the Windows release
toolchain, review their actual upstream notices as well. The Linux MinGW-w64
compiler in release CI is not version-pinned by REA: compare its installed
runtime/component notices with the retained snapshots and update them if they
differ. Do not assume that a compiler change leaves redistribution requirements
unchanged. Preserve applicable originals with any additionally bundled engine;
top-level reference copies alone may not cover its entire distribution.

Generate the exact locked inventory with `npm run licenses:generate`. After
refreshing verified runtime notices, update their header fingerprint to the
generator's reported `runtime_dependency_fingerprint`, then run
`npm run licenses:check`; `docs:check` also runs this check. It compares the
inventory, runtime package identities,
license declarations, archive URLs/integrity, runtime dependency fingerprint,
and preserved reference digests. It does not verify legal completeness or
replace inspection of original upstream notices.

("Apache 2.0").

/**
 * License object
 *
 * License information for the exposed API.
 *
 * @see {@link https://github.com/OAI/OpenAPI-Specification/blob/main/versions/3.1.2.md#license-object}
 */
export type LicenseObject = {
  /** **REQUIRED**. The license name used for the API. */
  name: string
  /** An [SPDX](https://spdx.org/licenses/) license expression for the API. The `identifier` field is mutually exclusive of the `url` field. */
  identifier?: string
  /** A URI for the license used for the API. This MUST be in the form of a URI. The `url` field is mutually exclusive of the `identifier` field. */
  url?: string
} & Record<`x-${string}`, unknown>

 * This code for `path.join` is directly copied from @zenfs/core/path for bundle size improvements.
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-3.0-or-later
 * Copyright (c) James Prevett and other ZenFS contributors.
 *
 * Windows support added:
 *   - Backslashes are normalised to forward slashes before processing.
 *   - Drive-letter prefixes (e.g. "C:") are detected and preserved through
 *     normalisation, so absolute Windows paths are handled correctly.
 *   - An absolute argument passed to join() resets the accumulated path,
 *     matching Node behaviour and handling worktree gitdir paths properly.
 *
 * Limitation: UNC paths (e.g. \\server\share) are not supported. The leading
 *   backslashes are normalised to forward slashes and then collapsed by
 *   normalizeString, losing the UNC root. Git on Windows works with
 *   drive-letter paths, so this is not expected to be a practical issue.
 */

free software--to make sure the software is free for all its users.

  This license, the Library General Public License, applies to some
specially designated Free Software Foundation software, and to any
other libraries whose authors decide to use it.  You can use it for
your libraries, too.

  When we speak of free software, we are referring to freedom, not
price.  Our General Public Licenses are designed to make sure that you
have the freedom to distribute copies of free software (and charge for
this service if you wish), that you receive source code or can get it
if you want it, that you can change the software or use pieces of it
in new free programs; and that you know you can do these things.

  To protect your rights, we need to make restrictions that forbid
anyone to deny you these rights or to ask you to surrender the rights.
These restrictions translate to certain responsibilities for you if
you distribute copies of the library, or if you modify it.

  For example, if you distribute copies of the library, whether gratis
or for a fee, you must give the recipients all the rights that we gave
you.  You must make sure that they, too, receive or can get the source
code.  If you link a program with the library, you must provide
complete object files to the recipients so that they can relink them
with the library, after making changes to the library and recompiling
it.  And you must show them these terms so they know their rights.

  Our method of protecting your rights has two steps: (1) copyright
the library, and (2) offer you this license which gives you legal
permission to copy, distribute and/or modify the library.

  Also, for each distributor's protection, we want to make certain
that everyone understands that there is no warranty for this free
library.  If the library is modified by someone else and passed on, we
want its recipients to know that what they have is not the original
version, so that any problems introduced by others will not reflect on
the original authors' reputations.

  Finally, any free program is threatened constantly by software
patents.  We wish to avoid the danger that companies distributing free
software will individually obtain patent licenses, thus in effect
transforming the program into proprietary software.  To prevent this,
we have made it clear that any patent must be licensed for everyone's
free use or not licensed at all.

  Most GNU software, including some libraries, is covered by the ordinary
GNU General Public License, which was designed for utility programs.  This
license, the GNU Library General Public License, applies to certain
designated libraries.  This license is quite different from the ordinary
one; be sure to read it in full, and don't assume that anything in it is
the same as in the ordinary license.

  The reason we have a separate public license for some libraries is that
they blur the distinction we usually make between modifying or adding to a
program and simply using it.  Linking a program with a library, without
changing the library, is in some sense simply using the library, and is
analogous to running a utility program or application program.  However, in
a textual and legal sense, the linked executable is a combined work, a
derivative of the original library, and the ordinary General Public License
treats it as such.

  Because of this blurred distinction, using the ordinary General
Public License for libraries did not effectively promote software
sharing, because most developers did not use the libraries.  We
concluded that weaker conditions might promote sharing better.

  However, unrestricted linking of non-free programs would deprive the
users of those programs of all benefit from the free status of the
libraries themselves.  This Library General Public License is intended to
permit developers of non-free programs to use free libraries, while
preserving your freedom as a user of such programs to change the free
libraries that are incorporated in them.  (We have not seen how to achieve
this as regards changes in header files, but we have achieved it as regards
changes in the actual functions of the Library.)  The hope is that this
will lead to faster development of free libraries.
